cohort: The study included 100 pregnant patients undergoing elective lower segment caesarean section with spinal anaesthesia.
finding: Spinal anaesthesia for elective caesarean section results in a statistically significant fall in maternal blood pressure (hypotension) and heart rate (bradycardia) due to arterial and venous vasodilatation and paradoxical activation of cardio inhibitory receptors.
cross-section timing: Intra-operative period, with measurements taken every 3 minutes for the first 20 minutes, then every 5 minutes until the end of surgery.
